name: Oksvik Fjordshell Anorak
description:
A pullover rain shell in a matte olive-grey fabric that sheds water like a second skin. The Fjordshell is cut long in the back, short in the front — a classic work-derived silhouette that keeps rain off your lower back without bunching when you sit. Single kangaroo chest pocket, drawstring hood that packs into its own collar, taped seams throughout. No insulation — this is a shell layer, worn over whatever you need underneath.

Oksvik is a mid-tier Scandinavian-heritage label now manufactured in the Milwaukee industrial district. Their stuff is functional and honest without being precious about it. The Fjordshell is what dock workers and infrastructure techs wear in the corridor's grey-season rains, and it's also what Tier 3 outdoor types buy because it actually works without advertising itself.
what_it_says: You care about staying dry more than you care about looking like you care about staying dry.
worn_by: anyone who walks to work in the rain
story_hooks: A particular batch of Fjordshells from the Milwaukee plant has a manufacturing defect — the DWR coating contains a trace compound that reacts with certain industrial runoff, staining the jacket a vivid rust-orange.
An infrastructure tech was last seen wearing an Oksvik Fjordshell before disappearing in a maintenance tunnel under the lakefront.
Oksvik's head of production has been quietly approached by a corponation looking to acquire the label — the workers on the floor have found out and aren't happy.
